Several functional criteria hard-require seed state: timer_changes (w2) needs unheld 'Probate estimate is 4,200 pounds.' shown at a 30-day M-13 timer; hold_scope_and_release (w2) needs 'Insurer letter acknowledged.' still held; deleted_message_takes_its_versions positive control and search_and_transcript rely on seed holds/versions. Seed read_up_to puts Dev at K-8 in M-13, so K-9 (Gwen's reply, 12 May 09:30) is already unread, and by criterion 13 earlier criteria have added unread M-13 messages from others: JUDGE-R0, R1, R2, R3, RX, R1B (nested_replies), JUDGE-E1 (edits), JUDGE-F1/F2 (safe_formatting). Under the only reasonable reading of 'where I stopped reading', the line belongs above K-9, not above JUDGE-U1. The golden does exactly that: app.js:186 'const firstUnread = r.data.messages.find(x => x.seq > r.data.last_read && !x.mine && !x.deleted)' with last_read = K-8's seq (server.js:119-122, 239-241). Reverse case: a broken app that always draws the line above the newest-arriving batch, ignoring the stored read position, would pass.

Secondary ambiguity (P2): walls-and-retention.md:19 says a new wall applies to someone with the matter open 'the next time their screen refreshes'. A second reasonable reading is a manual page reload; the live-update list in conversations.md:31 (posts, replies, edits, disappearing messages) does not name wall changes. Minor note (no defect claimed): conversations.md:29 requires same-time messages to have 'one consistent order', while sent_once_in_order Part B requires the send order A, B, C. Send order is the natural reading for chat, and conversations.md:7 says replies are kept 'in the order they were sent', so I treat this as acceptable. Separately, outside this row: hold_scope_and_release requires a delete refusal, but the first delete success (message_links) runs later, which conflicts with the prompt rule that a refusal pairs with an earlier or same-criterion success. Other row reviewers should check this.

With a flash model over OpenRouter through claude-code, each MCP round trip carrying chat-page snapshots plausibly costs ~8-15 s; 35-50 calls per heavy criterion spans ~300-750 s, straddling 520. The only comparator found (hosted Colderwater run run-outputs/coldwater-playground-devtools/runs-export/run-75888fe5.../result.json, verifier 08:21:34-09:29:53Z, ~68 min) used one BATCHED functional session, a different shape, so it does not measure per-criterion individual-mode duration here. That is standard rewardkit behaviour, not a task defect, but it makes the thin per-criterion headroom relevant. Plausible broken app passing / conforming app failing: a broken app gains nothing from these timeouts (timeouts only zero criteria). A conforming app (the golden) can lose credit if heavy criteria exceed 520 s with the configured judge - a credible, unmeasured risk rather than a demonstrated defect. No Oracle, model or portal score is claimed.
